title: rollout-runbook-checkin-notes-2026-04-06
content:
Date: 2026-04-06
Meeting: Rollout runbook check-in (weekly) — Console & Tooling
Owner: Aisha Patel
Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Claire, Diego, Samir, (notes: brief drop-ins from product: Lena)
Goal: Validate current canary runbook steps for the UI rollouts, confirm telemetry hooks for rollout analytics, and identify any pre-rollout blockers for tomorrow's small canary to 5% of traffic.

Agenda:
- Quick sync on canary criteria and metric thresholds
- UI feature flag orchestration (frontend + backend)
- Observability gaps (dashboards, alerting, tracing)
- Post-canary gating + rollback playbook verification
- Open blockers / owner assignment

Key notes / discussion highlights:
1) Canary thresholds and metric definitions- Primary metric: median server-side render latency for console routes (/projects, /deployments, /rollouts) — target <= 220ms at canary load.
- Secondary metrics: 95th percentile latency, error-rate (5xx) bump threshold +0.3% absolute, surface area: API times (model route), frontend error count (Sentry).
- Quality metric: feature flag surfaced via E2E smoke tests; if smoke tests fail twice in a row on canary, auto-abort.
- Marco: add a short pre-flight smoke suite run in CI that targets the exact canary environment (use canary DB snapshot).

2) UI feature flag orchestration- Claire: frontend flag rollout will use split-on-cookie + server-side guard in the console backend to avoid split mismatch.
- Need an explicit coordination event in the rollout orchestration: backend toggles first, then small wait window (30s), then frontend staged release. This reduces user-visible mismatch.
- Action: Claire -> add orchestration step to runbook + a small script to verify cookie propagation across LB nodes. Due: 2026-04-07 EOD.

3) Observability and telemetry hooks- Current gaps spotted: the rollout analytics dashboard doesn't show per-flag KPIs (we only have per-service). We want flag-specific funnels and error attribution.
- Diego: will add a per-flag tag on traces and metrics (span attribute flag_id, metric label: feature_flag). He notes some services instrumented differently (node backend vs go microservices) — will coordinate with infra team for consistent label names.
- Samir: will add SLO-based alert rules for canary: 95th latency breach (5% above baseline for 10 minutes) -> PagerDuty to oncall, and a separate non-pager Slack alert to #rollouts.
- Action: Diego + Samir -> prototype the flag-tagged dashboard and alert rules. Mock dashboard link will be posted in Slack by 2026-04-08.

4) Load shaping and traffic routing- Plan: tomorrow's canary is 5% traffic, weekday, low-traffic window (0900–1100 PT). Use smart routing to pin 5% to canary pool; fallback configured to default model variant.
- Note: routing policy needs to have a fallback mapping for models that have quantized variants — otherwise we saw prior errors where KV cache keys were incompatible. Marco will confirm model-variant compatibility list and add to runbook. Due: 2026-04-07.

5) Rollback playbook verification- Playbook steps reviewed: detect -> halt new canary assigns -> scale down canary pool -> trigger backend flag disable -> ensure session draining -> confirm stable baseline metrics -> record postmortem.
- Concern raised: previous rollback had a race where cache invalidation on canary nodes leaked into prod. Decision: add explicit cache clear step targeted by node ID range; verify via tracing that cache hits drop to 0 for canary sessions after rollback.
- Action: Samir -> add targeted cache-invalidation script to runbook and test in staging. Due: 2026-04-09.

6) E2E and load tests- We currently run a thin E2E suite; need one more targeted smoke that covers: flag toggles, ephemeral session cookie flows, and model fallback behavior.
- Action: Marco -> add 6 new E2E scenarios to the canary smoke. Run in CI against canary env before releasing. Due: 2026-04-07 08:00 PT (so we can gate the canary).

7) Analytics and post-rollout metrics collection- For post-canary evaluation, we agreed to capture a 45-minute window after ramp to 5%. Key artifacts: time-series export of latencies and error-rate, Sentry issue snapshots, and a quick UX survey ping for internal users (opt-in).
- Claire will prepare the post-rollout checklist for UX signals + where to get the survey results. Due: 2026-04-07 morning.

8) Runbook doc housekeeping- We identified outdated sections in the runbook: parts referencing old LB flags and a stale shepherd contact list. Aisha will prune and add an owner table with rotation notes.
- Action: Aisha -> update runbook owners table and change log; mark sections that must be reviewed each quarter. Due: 2026-04-10.

Open blockers (short):
- Infra: need confirmation that canary pool nodes have the new kernel patch (affects a perf regression we saw last month). Owner: Diego -> checking with infra team; update by 2026-04-06 18:00.
- QA: flaky smoke test in staging that occasionally times out. Owner: Claire -> triage and increase timeout for this specific test; follow-up 2026-04-07 morning.
- Data: missing historical baseline for a rare endpoint (GET /rollout/history). Owner: Marco -> fetch baseline via raw export and add to dashboard; due 2026-04-08.

Decisions made:
- Add explicit orchestration ordering (backend -> wait 30s -> frontend).
- Put per-flag telemetry tagging into production trace pipeline (feature_flag label).
- Require CI pre-flight E2E against canary snapshot before any traffic ramp.

Action items (summary):
- Claire: add orchestration step + cookie propagation script (due 2026-04-07 EOD).
- Marco: add 6 E2E canary scenarios + export baseline for history endpoint (due 2026-04-07 + 2026-04-08).
- Diego: flag-tag instrumentation + confirm kernel patch on canary nodes (prototype dashboard by 2026-04-08; infra check 2026-04-06).
- Samir: add SLO alerts + targeted cache-invalidation script (dashboard mock 2026-04-08; cache script 2026-04-09).
- Aisha: update runbook owners table and change log (2026-04-10).

Notes to self / informal fragments:
- "If the canary shows a small 95th pctl bump but not errors, skip rollback but scale back to 2% for 30m and re-evaluate." (add as a conditional step in runbook).
- Remember to call out the UX survey to internal beta users (Slack #internal-beta).
- Re-check that the model-variant fallback mapping is symmetrical across regions — last time APAC had a missing mapping that silently failed.

Next check-in: 2026-04-07 08:30 PT quick go/no-go sync (15m) before canary start.

Attached references / useful links (copied into runbook):
- PR for frontend split logic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1489
- Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/ENGCON-237 (canary automation epic)
- Runbook home: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Runbook+-+Canary+Rollouts

Status: draft notes from meeting; will update after 04-07 go/no-go.

-- end of notes --
